accepted.s: In June 2023, an expert committee under which Ministry identified 30 critical minerals for India?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: An expert committee under the Ministry of Mines identified 30 critical minerals in June 2023.
accepted.tq: Identify the responsible ministry rather than confusing it with a related sectoral ministry.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: Coking coal has been notified as a Critical and Strategic Mineral under which legislation?
o: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957
accepted.x: Coking coal has been notified as a Critical and Strategic Mineral under the MMDR Act, 1957.
accepted.tq: Match the mineral notification with the correct statutory framework.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding coking coal in India:
1. More than 90 per cent of its reserves are located in Jharia.
2. It has been notified as a Critical and Strategic Mineral.
3. Its notification was made under the MMDR Act, 1957.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: coking coal is a notified critical and strategic mineral under the MMDR Act, 1957, and over 90 per cent of its reserves are in Jharia.
accepted.tq: Check whether all statements belong to the same mineral-policy fact cluster.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the target of the National Critical Mineral Mission for domestic exploration by 2030–31?
accepted.x: The National Critical Mineral Mission targets 1,200 domestic exploration projects by 2030–31.
accepted.tq: Use the precise target figure and distinguish it from nearby rounded estimates.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Critical Mineral Mission targets the development of at least how many critical minerals and acquisition of how many overseas assets?
accepted.x: The mission targets output of at least 15 critical minerals and 50 overseas assets.
accepted.tq: Separate paired numerical targets instead of relying on the larger list of 30 critical minerals.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: KABIL, the company associated with overseas acquisition of critical mineral assets, is a joint venture of which organisations?
accepted.x: KABIL is a joint venture of National Aluminium Company Limited, Hindustan Copper Limited and Mineral Exploration Corporation Limited.
accepted.tq: Test composition by identifying the exact public-sector partners.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: KABIL holds an area of 15,703 hectares for lithium exploration in which Argentine province?
accepted.x: KABIL holds 15,703 hectares in Catamarca, Argentina, for lithium exploration.
accepted.tq: Combine the exact area figure with its geographic location.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The rare-earth corridors proposed in the Union Budget 2026–27 include which of the following States?
1. Odisha
2. Kerala
3. Andhra Pradesh
4. Tamil Nadu
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The proposed rare-earth corridors cover Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
accepted.tq: Verify the complete geographical list before selecting a partial combination.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: When was the India–United States framework on critical minerals and rare earths signed?
accepted.x: The India–US critical minerals and rare earths framework was signed in May 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the month-year pairing to separate bilateral frameworks from other agreements.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the auction of critical and strategic mineral blocks?
o: 50 blocks were sold in six tranches, and the seventh tranche of 19 blocks opened on 23 May 2026.
46 blocks were sold in seven tranches, and the eighth tranche of 19 blocks opened on 23 March 2026.
19 blocks were sold in six tranches, and the seventh tranche of 46 blocks opened on 23 March 2026.
46 blocks were sold in six tranches, and the seventh tranche of 19 blocks opened on 23 March 2026.
accepted.x: A total of 46 critical and strategic blocks were sold in six tranches; the seventh tranche, comprising 19 blocks, opened on 23 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Check the sequence, tranche number, block count and date together.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Critical Mineral Recycling Incentive Scheme has an allocation of ₹1,500 crore for which period?
accepted.x: The scheme has an allocation of ₹1,500 crore for FY2025–26 to FY2030–31.
accepted.tq: Read the financial-year endpoints precisely rather than treating the scheme as annual.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are covered by the Critical Mineral Recycling Incentive Scheme?
1. E-waste
2. Lithium-ion batteries
3. Other scrap
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Central Sector scheme covers e-waste, lithium-ion batteries and other scrap.
accepted.tq: Look for the complete list of covered waste streams, including the broad residual category.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s partnership with Australia announced in 2022 concerning critical minerals primarily relates to which minerals?
accepted.x: India’s 2022 partnership with Australia concerns lithium and cobalt.
accepted.tq: Use the partner–mineral association rather than selecting common Indian mineral pairs.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which country is identified as India’s largest supplier of minerals, mainly copper, among the following?
accepted.x: Chile is identified as India’s largest supplier, mainly of copper.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between countries involved in exploration partnerships and the principal supplier.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: The ‘Uncover India’ project is being undertaken by GSI in collaboration with which organisation to probe deep-seated deposits?
accepted.x: GSI’s ‘Uncover India’ project is being carried out with Geoscience Australia to probe deep-seated deposits.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact international technical partner in a bilateral scientific project.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a tool of the National Critical Mineral Mission?
o: Recovery of minerals from overburden and tailings
A ban on acquisition of mineral assets abroad
accepted.x: The mission supports PSU and private acquisition of mineral assets abroad; it does not ban such acquisition. Recovery from waste, fast-track approvals and a national stockpile are listed tools.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated policy instrument.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the recent MMDR amendment, a State must approve adding a critical mineral to a lease within what period?
accepted.x: States must approve the addition of a critical mineral to a lease within 30 days.
accepted.tq: Test the statutory time limit using closely spaced numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the recent MMDR amendment is correct?
o: It abolished mineral leases for critical minerals.
It introduced captive-sale limits for all critical minerals.
It transferred approval power from States to district administrations.
accepted.x: The recent amendment removed captive-sale limits and also requires State approval for adding a critical mineral to a lease within 30 days.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a removal of a restriction from its introduction or expansion.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, comprehensive mineral mapping for critical and high-value deposits has been ordered with value addition through which agency?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Mineral Development Corporation (APMDC) is to facilitate value addition following comprehensive mineral mapping.
accepted.tq: Identify the specialised State agency associated with mineral development.
accepted.sec: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL) [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which rock system is regarded as the oldest in India, with an age of more than 2,500 million years?
accepted.x: The Archaean or Dharwar system is the oldest, being more than 2,500 million years old, and is metamorphosed.
accepted.tq: Use the age clue to distinguish the oldest rock system from younger formations.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets of minerals is associated with the Archaean or Dharwar system?
o: Iron ore, manganese, gold and copper
Sandstone, limestone, building stone and Panna diamonds
accepted.x: The Archaean or Dharwar system contains iron ore, manganese, gold and copper.
accepted.tq: Match the rock system with its characteristic mineral association.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Cuddapah rock system derives its name from which place in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The Cuddapah system is named after Kadapa in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test the geographical origin of a geological nomenclature.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following series of the Vindhyan system from lower to upper:
A. Rewa
B. Semri
C. Bhander
D. Kaimur
accepted.x: The Vindhyan series from lower to upper are Semri, Kaimur, Rewa and Bhander.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last layers, then place the intermediate series in sequence.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is associated with the Vindhyan rock system?
1. Sandstone
2. Limestone
3. Panna diamonds
4. Building stone
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Vindhyan system contains sandstone, limestone, building stone and Panna diamonds.
accepted.tq: Check the complete mineral-and-rock list before accepting a partial code.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Gondwana rock system is best associated with which geological period and resource?
o: Permo-Carboniferous period and bulk of India’s coal
accepted.x: The Gondwana system is Permo-Carboniferous and contains the bulk of India’s coal, particularly in the Damodar and Mahanadi basins.
accepted.tq: Combine the geological age with the dominant economic resource.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Damodar and Mahanadi basins are particularly associated with which rock system?
accepted.x: The Damodar and Mahanadi basins are important Gondwana formations and contain major coal resources.
accepted.tq: Match the named basins with their geological system.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Deccan Trap?
o: It is approximately 65 million years old and consists of end-Cretaceous basalt.
It is an Archaean metamorphosed system older than 2,500 million years.
It is a Tertiary system associated mainly with petroleum of Assam and Gujarat.
It is a Permo-Carboniferous system containing most of India’s coal.
accepted.x: The Deccan Trap is approximately 65 million years old and consists of basalt formed at the end of the Cretaceous.
accepted.tq: Use the age and rock type together to distinguish the Deccan Trap from other systems.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s: Younger coal and lignite, including Neyveli lignite, and the petroleum resources of Assam and Gujarat are associated with which rock system?
accepted.x: The Tertiary system is associated with younger coal and lignite, including Neyveli, and petroleum in Assam and Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Match the resource profile with the correct geological system.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s: Khondalite belongs to which geological association?
o: A Vindhyan series of the Cuddapah system
An Eastern Ghats series of the Archaean system
accepted.x: Khondalite is an Eastern Ghats series belonging to the Archaean system; it is not a Vindhyan formation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the look-alike geological classifications of Khondalite and Vindhyan rocks.
accepted.sec: Rock systems of India → series and minerals [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mica generally occurs in which form and host-rock setting?
o: In limestone caves and river terraces
In pegmatite veins in granite, gneiss and schist
As layers in basalt and sandstone only
accepted.x: Mica occurs in pegmatite veins hosted by granite, gneiss and schist.
accepted.tq: Match the mineral occurrence with its characteristic host rocks.
accepted.sec: Mica - host rocks and associated minerals, top states and mines [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which pair represents the principal varieties or minerals of mica?
accepted.x: Phlogopite and muscovite are the main mica minerals; phlogopite is magnesium mica.
accepted.tq: Separate mica varieties from iron, carbonate and titanium mineral pairs.
accepted.sec: Mica - host rocks and associated minerals, top states and mines [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly lists the major mica belts of India?
1. Nellore in Andhra Pradesh
2. Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh in Jharkhand–Bihar
3. Ajmer–Bhilwara in Rajasthan
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The major mica belts are Nellore, Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh and Ajmer–Bhilwara.
accepted.tq: Verify each belt–State association before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Mica - host rocks and associated minerals, top states and mines [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh was historically famous for mica?
accepted.x: Nellore was historically famous for mica and forms one of the principal mica belts of India.
accepted.tq: Use the mineral-belt location to identify the correct Andhra Pradesh district.
accepted.sec: Mica - host rocks and associated minerals, top states and mines [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mica is widely used in electrical and electronic industries primarily because it functions as a/an:
accepted.x: Mica is used in electrical and electronic industries because it is an effective electrical insulator.
accepted.tq: Infer the industrial use from the defining physical property.
accepted.sec: Mica - host rocks and associated minerals, top states and mines [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the minerals associated with SPSR Nellore?
accepted.x: SPSR Nellore is associated with quartz, feldspar, silica sand and vermiculite; bauxite is not included in this listed association.
accepted.tq: Find the mineral outside the specific district association rather than selecting a common mineral at random.
accepted.sec: Mica - host rocks and associated minerals, top states and mines [APPSC]
